quadHead: The same pressure patterns — in every country.

quad.title: Airport Black-Taxi Switch
quad.tl: A ¥120–180 ride to your hotel ticks up to ¥600 — “night rate, traffic surcharge, special road.”

quad.title: The Scippatori Moped Snatch
quad.tl: A two-rider Vespa accelerates past on Via Toledo and the passenger tears the bag or watch off you in one motion — one British tourist lost a €35,000 Rolex from his wrist in broad daylight.

quad.title: The Fake Police ID Check
quad.tl: Two men near the Grand Bazaar flash laminated badges, claim a counterfeit-currency check, separate your passport from your wallet — and hand the passport back short of cash.

quad.title: Airport No-Meter Taxi
quad.tl: A man in an orange vest steers you past the rank to a curbside sedan quoting a flat 50 dollars to Zamalek — the metered fare is 150–250 EGP.

desc.price: THE BIG BOOK · TRAVEL SAFETY SERIES
body: The Big Book of Travel Scams is the master volume of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series — the thirty scams that recur, in one form or another, almost everywhere you travel. Every entry is documented against press and police records, embassy advisories, and verified traveler reports.

Thirty scams across twenty-four countries, organized around the seven universal pressure patterns. The exact scripts, the red flags that give each away, and exit phrases in eleven languages you can show on your phone.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched and updated every year — when a new edition ships, it appears in your Kindle library. One field guide for the whole trip, wherever it goes.
